title: Which two small numbers meet only after fifty?
description: Two numbers below ten are given to idli and vada, and the first idli-vada comes after fifty. Pairs with a small number meet early, so only the pairs from seven, eight and nine fit.
teaching_notes: One idea: the first idli-vada is where the two lists of multiples first meet, and big numbers meet late. Watch for students who give only one pair.

source: Figure it Out box 2, Q6, p.111
video_script.why: The child finds the pairs of numbers below ten whose lists of multiples first meet after fifty.
video_script.substitution: Write the lists of multiples of a pair and find where they first meet.
video_script.anchor: Ruhee and friends playing the idli-vada game with two numbers below ten
video_script.payoff_line: The numbers could be seven and eight, eight and nine, or seven and nine

final_answer.spoken: the numbers could be seven and eight, eight and nine, or seven and nine

names.Ruhee: plays the idli-vada game with friends

hold_back: seven and eight, eight and nine
maths_rules: the first idli-vada is the first number in both lists of multiples; it must be more than 50
pairs using a number below 7 meet before 50 (5 and 9 at 45, 6 and 7 at 42)
check: all three pairs are below 10 and 56, 72, 63 are above 50
video_script.design: One idea: the first idli-vada is where two lists of multiples first meet, and big numbers meet late. Same method as the book example: write both lists and find the first number in both.
